title: Termination of the power of acceptance
shortTitle: Termination of the power of acceptance
summary: The chapter separates lapse, revocation, rejection, and death or incapacity, then considers communication timing.
notes: An offer can expire by its stated limit or a reasonable time. Revocation is the offeror’s withdrawal and normally requires communication; public offers create a publicity problem. Rejection is the offeree’s act and is distinct from mere inquiry. Death and incapacity have specified effects for ordinary offers, with an option-contract qualification. The mailbox rule addresses when an otherwise proper acceptance becomes effective, rather than whether the response contains assent.
